units.text: Why More Games Isn't Enough
Built, then measured.

More playing time feels like the answer. Another season, another team, more reps in real games. And a year later, the same kid, the same speed.
Here's the brutal truth. A game doesn't develop an athlete. It reveals one. It shows you exactly what was built in training and nothing more, so playing more games just runs the same ceiling out there again and again under pressure.
That's the difference our Multi-Sport Foundation Program is built on. We develop the engine, the speed and power a game can only put on display, which means a first step that beats the defender to the ball, more touches every game, and the kind of play that makes coaches start asking who that kid is.
The first step in is the Athlete Analysis. We run your athlete through the same timing gates and velocity trackers we use every session, and you walk out with their real sprint time and jump numbers. Not a tryout. A data set.
Then the guarantee: +1 mph. +3 inches. 90 days. Or we keep training them free.

More playing time feels like the answer. Another season, another team, more reps in real games. And a year later, the same kid, the same speed.
Here's the brutal truth. A game is a test, not a teacher. Why More Games Isn't Enough
Built, then measured.

More playing time feels like the answer. Another season, another team, more reps in real games. And a year later, the same kid, the same speed.
Here's the brutal truth. A game is a test, not a teacher. Everything your kid does on the field, the first step, the closing speed, the burst to the ball, got built somewhere else, and the game simply hands back the result. When a kid isn't fast enough, more games keep grading the same engine and reporting the same score. The ceiling never moves, because nothing on a game field was ever designed to move it.
That's why a whole season can pass with nothing to show for it. Your kid plays out the athlete they already were in September, and then does it again the following fall.
And here's something worth saying plainly: none of that playing time was wasted, and you weren't wrong to want it. Games matter. They're where a kid competes, learns to read the field, and finds out what they're made of under pressure. They were just never the place an athlete gets built, and asking a game to make a kid faster is asking the scoreboard to do the work of the weight room.
Building the engine is a separate job, and it's the one our Multi-Sport Foundation Program exists to do. It runs on The Velocity Code™, and every session we develop the real sprint speed and explosive power a game can only put on display, measured on purpose, rep by rep.
That kind of speed doesn't stay in the gym. It becomes the first step that beats the defender to the ball. That turns into more touches every single game. More touches become the plays that change the score, and those plays become the film a coach actually stops to watch, until one season in, the kid who used to blend into the roster is the one getting asked about by name.
One dad told us his son had been somewhere else for two years, and that a single week with us was enough for the kid to say it was the best he'd ever had. The reason was simple. He could feel that he was finally being built, not just put through his paces and sent home.
The first step in is the Athlete Analysis. We run your athlete through the same Dashr timing gates and GymAware velocity trackers the NFL uses, and you leave with their real sprint time, real jump height, and a clear picture of where they stand. Not a tryout. A data set you get to keep. From there, the path into the Multi-Sport Foundation Program is simple.
Coach Graham Wilkerson built this. He's a CSCS, the same credential D1 and NFL strength coaches carry, and he trained NFL athletes Zack Martin, Ted Karras, and Nick Martin before adapting these principles for the developmental window where they matter most.
Here's the promise no other program in this market will make. +1 mph. +3 inches. 90 days. Or we keep training them free until they get there.

ad-3.bodyLine.4.4.text: They were just never the place an athlete gets built, and asking a game to make a kid faster is asking the scoreboard to do the work of the weight room.

ad-3.bodyPara.5.text: Building the engine is a separate job, and it's the one our Multi-Sport Foundation Program exists to do. It runs on The Velocity Code™, and every session we develop the real sprint speed and explosive power a game can only put on display, measured on purpose, rep by rep.

ad-3.bodyPara.6.text: That kind of speed doesn't stay in the gym. It becomes the first step that beats the defender to the ball. That turns into more touches every single game. More touches become the plays that change the score, and those plays become the film a coach actually stops to watch, until one season in, the kid who used to blend into the roster is the one getting asked about by name.

ad-3.altHook.1.text: Your kid can play a hundred games this year and finish exactly as fast as they started. Here's why.

ad-3.altHook.2.text: Games don't make athletes faster. They just show you how fast training already made them.

ad-3.altHook.3.text: More game film won't fix a speed problem. It'll just record it in higher definition.
